CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate regression bisection outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. Re-check edge cases relevant to regression bisection (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
3. Keep regression bisection changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. Measure before optimizing any regression bisection bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
5. When regression bisection guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
6. Document any non-obvious regression bisection decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
7. Keep regression bisection outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
8. When multiple regression bisection strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
9. Before starting regression bisection work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop regression bisection edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated regression bisection concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not skip documenting regression bisection assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of regression bisection correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these regression bisection guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
